title: Calculus — Mission 1: The Rate of Change
description: Launch control lost the velocity feed on Meridian's test rocket. You have one telemetry window to prove you understand what a derivative actually measures before the next burn.

priya.name: Dr. Priya Anand
priya.description: Reads position-time graphs the way most people read text messages.

sam.name: Sam
sam.description: Keeps calling acceleration 'the speed of the speed.'

graph_pad.name: Graphing Pad
graph_pad.description: Plots position, velocity, and acceleration curves live.

chart.name: Telemetry Chart
chart.description: The rocket's raw position-vs-time data from the last burn.

elements.text: Our velocity readout died mid-ascent. All we have left is the raw position-time data.
Can't we just... look at how high it is right now and call it good?

options.text: "Position alone won't tell us speed. We need the derivative — the instantaneous rate of change of position."
"Just divide the total height by the total time. Close enough."

elements.text: Good instinct grabbing the chart. Let's see if you can actually read it.
Averages hide the moment the engine actually struggled. We need more than that.

config.question: The rocket's height is given by h(t). What does h'(t) represent at a specific time t?

options.text: The instantaneous velocity of the rocket at time t
The total distance traveled up to time t
The average height over the whole flight
The area under the height curve

config.explanation: The derivative of a position function at a point gives the instantaneous rate of change — velocity — at that exact moment.

config.prompt: Order these from the rocket's raw measurement to the most 'derived' quantity.
Sam: "If h(t) = 3t^2, what's h'(t)? Type it using ^ for powers, like 6t."

elements.text: Velocity's reconstructed from the position data. We can clear the next burn.
We patched it together. Next time, start with the derivative, not the guess.

options.text: Walk Sam through why derivatives beat averages for real-time control.
Sign off. The burn is cleared — that's enough for today.

elements.text: So velocity is the slope of position, and acceleration is the slope of velocity. It's slopes all the way down.

ending.title: Rate of Change Hero
ending.description: Rebuilt the telemetry feed and taught the team what a derivative is actually for.

ending.title: Burn Cleared
ending.description: The rocket flies. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
